newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi propaganda chiefs criticise lavish weddings.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi propaganda chiefs criticise lavish weddings.

text.p: Propaganda chiefs in Vietnam's leafy capital have lashed out at lavish spending on wedding ceremonies and are considering ways to make marriage ceremonies more solemn.

Wednesday's Saigon Times Daily said Hanoi's Communist Party Propaganda and Science Board met last weekend and "severely criticised the tendency to commcercialise weddings and the trend to hold lavish and boastful ceremonies".
"They suggested launching a campaign to devise and put into practise ways to organise happy, solemn civilised and economical wedding ceremonies," the newspaper said.
The report did not say if the participants were married.
Vietnam is one of the poorest countries in the world.
Traditionally weddings are paid for by the families of the couples involved, but in recent years it has become common practice to accept cash donations from guests.
